account:
It is day 1, just after seven in the morning, and I am at town hall with the secretary. I have received a book titled 'Appointment requests' but have not yet read it. My remembered schedule includes a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, afternoon office business and tea with the neighbour, and an eighteen-to-eighteen-thirty meeting in the great hall. The secretary says she will escort me to that meeting.

The unusual business is the hospitality planning involving the innkeeper, builder and freight operator. They describe its purpose as practical arrangements for community gatherings: refreshments, deliveries and hall lighting. The innkeeper explicitly told me residents are welcome and need not prepare anything. The neighbour intends to attend. I also saw a lantern installed in the hall yesterday, which could fit the lighting arrangements, although I do not know who installed it or why.

The most striking new information is the secretary's report that the baker says this committee ordered 120 loaves, baked yesterday, with payment still unconfirmed. She says she has authorized no payment. That is a substantial order, and I do not yet know the intended gathering, who agreed to pay, or whether these loaves are meant for tonight or another occasion. I should establish those facts rather than assume public funds are committed.

Yesterday there was speculation about lights and possible celebration news. The neighbour said the baker explained the oven glow, and had no confirmed customer name or date. The large bread order now suggests preparations for a sizeable gathering, but that remains an inference, not proof of a secret celebration or wrongdoing. The committee has answered my questions about membership, agenda and public attendance, yet the specific occasion and financial arrangements remain unclear. I want to read the book and clarify those details with the secretary and the people involved.
